articles.title: The Settings gear: what is in it
articles.summary: The gear at the top right opens a drop-down with your licence, the look of the app, options such as Export ZIP, Training Wheels and File Picker, quick tools, spec-map import and Auto-deploy.
articles.what: The Settings gear (top right) opens one drop-down. From top to bottom: License (shows your licence status), LOOKS (the visual theme of the booth), Options (Export ZIP Package, Training Wheels, a light or dark toggle, the File Picker choice, and a Report a Problem button that copies a diagnostic report without your licence key), Quick Tools (Keyboard Shortcuts), Import Spec Map (merge mode) with a Clear button, and Auto-Deploy to iRacing. This is different from the gear inside the AI panel, which holds your AI key, model and Claude/ChatGPT connection.
when: You want to turn Auto-deploy on or off.
You want a different look for the app, or the Windows file chooser.
You need to report a problem or see the shortcuts.
how: Click the gear at the top right of the booth.
Scroll to the section you want, change it, and click outside the drop-down (or press the gear again) to close it.
Settings are remembered on this computer.

controls.label: Export ZIP Package
controls.effect: Builds one ZIP of paint TGA, spec TGA and preview on every render. The ZIP stays in that render's own job folder and is offered as a Download ZIP Package link under the render; it is never copied into the iRacing car folder, which only receives the TGA files.

controls.label: Training Wheels
controls.effect: Quests and a next-move hint chip that teach the app while you use it.

controls.label: Auto-deploy after render
controls.effect: A second, optional push of each render to the visible iRacing Car Folder or a saved active car; a car folder set in the header already receives every render without it.

controls.label: Import Spec Map
controls.effect: Merges an existing spec TGA under your zones; Clear removes it.

tips: To avoid overwriting a paint you like in iRacing while you experiment, leave the iRacing Car Folder box in the header empty and Auto-deploy off. As soon as a car folder is set, every render is copied into it, whether Auto-deploy is on or not.
The gear in the AI panel is separate: that one has the AI key and the Claude/ChatGPT connection.
pitfalls: An imported spec map stays under every render until you press Clear.
Report a Problem makes text for you to paste to support; it does not send anything by itself.

deep.heading: The drop-down from top to bottom
deep.body: License shows your licence status. LOOKS changes the theme of the booth. Options holds Export ZIP Package, Training Wheels, the dark/light toggle, the File Picker choice and Report a Problem. Quick Tools holds Keyboard Shortcuts. Import Spec Map merges an existing shine file under your zones, with a Clear button. Auto-Deploy to iRacing is only a second, optional push of each render, to the visible iRacing Car Folder or a saved active car; a car folder set in the header is already filled by every render without it. Everything is remembered on this computer.

deep.heading: Two different gears
deep.body: The gear at the top right is the booth settings. The AI panel has its own gear, which holds the AI key, the model and the Claude or ChatGPT connection. Mixing them up is the most common reason people cannot find the key box.

deep.heading: Settings that change your files, and settings that do not
deep.body: Looks, light/dark, File Picker and Training Wheels only change how the booth behaves. Three options touch your output: Export ZIP Package adds a ZIP with the paint TGA, spec TGA and preview on every render (kept in the render's job folder, with a download link); Auto-Deploy is only a second, optional push (an iRacing Car Folder set in the header already receives every render); and an imported spec map stays under every render until you press Clear.

examples.title: Safe experimenting setup
examples.goal: Try ideas without overwriting a paint you like in iRacing
examples.result: Every render makes a ZIP in its own job folder, with a download link under the render. Nothing reaches iRacing while the iRacing Car Folder box in the header is empty; with a car folder set, every render copies its TGAs there whether Auto-Deploy is on or off.

examples.title: Ready to race
examples.goal: Get each finished render straight into the sim
examples.result: The render lands in the car folder and the sim reloads the car textures.

faq.q: Where is the key box for the AI?
faq.a: In the gear inside the AI panel, not in the booth Settings gear.

faq.q: Are my settings saved?
faq.a: Yes, on this computer. A different computer starts with the defaults.

faq.q: Does Report a Problem send anything?
faq.a: No. It copies a report for you to paste to support, and the report never includes your licence key.

faq.q: Why is there an old spec showing in every render?
faq.a: You imported a spec map. It stays under every render until you press Clear next to Import Spec Map.

faq.q: Can I change the language of the app?
faq.a: No. Shokker Paint Booth is in English only and the Settings gear has no language option. The LOOKS choice changes the colours of the app, not the language.

mistakes.symptom: Your iRacing paint was overwritten by an experiment
mistakes.cause: The iRacing Car Folder was set while you were testing (every render is copied into it), or Auto-Deploy was on
mistakes.fix: Clear the iRacing Car Folder box and keep Auto-Deploy off while experimenting; set the folder again when you are happy.

mistakes.symptom: Every render has a strange shine you did not set
mistakes.cause: An imported spec map is still merged under your zones
mistakes.fix: Open Settings and press Clear beside Import Spec Map, then render again.

protips: Turn on Export ZIP Package for a project you care about. Each render then leaves you a dated bundle of paint, spec and preview to go back to.

articles.title: File Picker: Shokker Browser or Windows File Explorer
articles.summary: Choose which file chooser opens for Source Paint, layered paint and the iRacing Car Folder: the Shokker Browser with image previews, or the normal Windows File Explorer.
articles.what: In Settings > Options, the File Picker setting decides how the Source Paint, Open Layered and iRacing Folder buttons let you pick things. Shokker Browser is the default and shows image previews, which is handy for TGA artwork. Windows File Explorer opens the standard Windows chooser, which some people find more familiar. The choice is saved on this computer. It works in the desktop app and also when you run the booth in a browser tab, because the server runs on the same machine and opens the Windows dialog for you.
when: You prefer the Windows chooser, or need a network drive that the Shokker Browser does not show.
The chooser looks wrong or you cannot find a folder.
how: Open the File Picker list and pick Shokker Browser or Windows File Explorer.
Click Source Paint (or Open Layered, or the iRacing Folder button) to try it.

controls.label: File Picker
controls.effect: Which chooser opens for Source Paint, layered paint and the iRacing folder.

tips: Use Windows File Explorer if you need to type or paste a path, or browse to a folder on another drive.
pitfalls: The picker setting does not change the files themselves, only how you choose them.
The Windows chooser may open behind the booth window; Alt+Tab to find it.

deep.heading: What each chooser gives you
deep.body: Shokker Browser is the default. It shows image previews, which is handy for TGA artwork you cannot recognise by name. Windows File Explorer opens the standard Windows chooser, where you can type or paste a path or browse to another drive. It is used for Source Paint, Open Layered and the iRacing Folder button.

deep.heading: Why it also works in a browser tab
deep.body: The booth's server runs on your own PC, so even in a browser tab it can open the real Windows dialog for you. The choice is saved on this computer.

deep.heading: What it does not change
deep.body: The picker only changes how you choose a file. Your files, the render and the colours are identical either way.

examples.title: Use a network or second drive
examples.goal: Open artwork that lives on another drive

settings.Then: Click Source Paint and browse or paste the path

examples.result: The Windows chooser opens, and you can type the full path to the file.

examples.title: Go back to previews
examples.goal: See image thumbnails while picking TGA artwork
examples.result: The next file chooser shows image previews.

faq.q: The Windows chooser did not appear. Where is it?
faq.a: It may have opened behind the booth window. Press Alt+Tab to find it.

faq.q: I cannot find my folder in the Shokker Browser.
faq.a: Switch to Windows File Explorer and type or paste the path, or browse to the other drive.

faq.q: Does it change my files?
faq.a: No. It changes only how you pick them.

mistakes.symptom: You click Source Paint and nothing seems to open
mistakes.cause: The Windows chooser opened behind the booth
mistakes.fix: Press Alt+Tab, or switch the File Picker back to Shokker Browser.

mistakes.symptom: Your network drive is not listed
mistakes.cause: The Shokker Browser does not show every drive
mistakes.fix: Use Windows File Explorer and paste the path.

protips: If you are going to open many TGA files in a row, keep the Shokker Browser. Previews save you from opening the wrong file.

articles.title: Looks, light or dark, and Training Wheels
articles.summary: Settings lets you change the look of the app (Classic plus 15 themes), switch between dark and light, and turn the Training Wheels quests on or off.
articles.what: LOOKS in the Settings drop-down changes the colours and shapes of the booth: Classic Mode is the default, and 15 more looks include Pro Dark, Linear, Nord, Dracula, Monokai, Solarized Dark, Carbon, OLED Black, Graphite, Studio Warm, Midnight Navy, Emerald Pro, Copper, High Contrast and Compact Pro. Switching is instant and the choice is remembered. A Light button next to it switches between dark and light. Training Wheels is the switch for the quest engine: step-by-step quests and a next-move hint chip that teach you the app as you work. Finishing the Core Loop offers to turn it off. None of this changes your paint.
when: The booth is hard to read on your monitor.
You are new and want guidance, or experienced and want the hints gone.
how: Under LOOKS, click a look; it applies at once.
Use the Light button if you need a light theme.
Under Options, switch Training Wheels off when you no longer want hints.

controls.label: Look
controls.effect: Changes the booth's colours and shapes only.

controls.label: Training Wheels
controls.effect: Quests and hint chip that teach the app.

tips: High Contrast is the easiest to read.
If the booth looks cramped, try Compact Pro or check the UI size in the panels article.
pitfalls: The white modes (Pro Light, Paper, Spacious) were retired; a saved choice of a retired look falls back to Classic.
aliases: change the look of the app

deep.heading: Sixteen looks, all instant
deep.body: Classic Mode is the default, and 15 more looks are Pro Dark, Linear, Nord, Dracula, Monokai, Solarized Dark, Carbon, OLED Black, Graphite, Studio Warm, Midnight Navy, Emerald Pro, Copper, High Contrast and Compact Pro. Switching applies at once and is remembered. A Light button switches between dark and light. None of it changes your paint, only the colours and shapes of the booth.

deep.heading: Retired looks
deep.body: The white modes (Pro Light, Paper, Spacious) were retired. If you saved one of them earlier, the booth falls back to Classic instead of breaking.

deep.heading: Training Wheels
deep.body: Training Wheels is the switch for step-by-step quests and a next-move hint chip that teach the app while you work. Finishing the Core Loop offers to turn it off. It is off until you choose to turn it on.

examples.title: Easier on the eyes
examples.goal: Make the booth readable on a hard-to-read monitor

settings.Light button: Try it if the screen is bright

examples.result: High Contrast is the easiest look to read.

examples.title: More room for the car
examples.goal: Fit more on a small screen
examples.result: Tighter panels leave more room for the preview.

faq.q: Does a look change my paint?
faq.a: No. It only changes the booth's colours and shapes.

faq.q: How do I get rid of the hints?
faq.a: Switch Training Wheels off in Options, or finish the Core Loop and accept the offer to turn it off.

faq.q: The booth looks cramped.
faq.a: Try Compact Pro, or change the UI size in the panels settings.

faq.q: My saved look disappeared.
faq.a: If it was one of the retired white modes, the booth fell back to Classic. Pick another look.

mistakes.symptom: You look for a white theme and cannot find it
mistakes.fix: Use the Light button next to LOOKS for a light theme.
Turn it off in Settings, Options.

protips: Pick the look first, then the UI size. A look that fits your monitor saves more eye strain than any other setting.

articles.title: Your licence: activating, offline and a new PC
articles.summary: Your licence key is entered when the desktop app starts. The app checks it online, saves it for this PC, and asks again if you move to another PC or Windows account.
articles.what: When you first start the desktop app a licence window asks for your key. The app checks the key with the seller's licence service and, if it is good, saves an encrypted licence file for this computer. If the service cannot be reached, the app saves an offline activation instead and lets you in. The saved licence is tied to this PC and Windows user, so on another PC, or if the Windows account changes, the app asks for your key again. After that, the Settings gear shows your licence status; in current builds it shows License Active and the key box is hidden because activation already happened at start-up. If you cannot activate, check the key for typos and your internet, and use Report a Problem.
when: You moved to a new PC or reinstalled Windows.
The app keeps asking for a key.
how: Start the app. In the licence window, paste your key and click Activate.
Wait for Verifying. If your internet is down, the app says it saved an offline activation.
On a new PC, enter the same key again. If it is refused as already used, contact support and say which PC the key was used on.
No key yet? The same window has a Buy License button.

controls.label: License key
controls.effect: Your purchased key. Pasted at start-up.

controls.label: Activate
controls.effect: Checks the key and saves it for this PC.

controls.label: Deactivate
controls.effect: Removes the activation from this PC so the key can be used elsewhere.

tips: Keep the message or receipt that has your key.
Type or paste the key without extra spaces.
pitfalls: Activation is per PC and Windows user. A reinstall that keeps your Windows account does not need a new key, but a different PC does.
Do not share your key in screenshots or support text; Report a Problem never includes it.
aliases: it asks for my key again
how many pcs can i install on

deep.heading: What happens at start-up
deep.body: The licence window asks for your key. The app checks it with the seller's licence service and, if it is good, saves an encrypted licence file for this computer. If the service cannot be reached, it saves an offline activation instead and lets you in.

deep.heading: Tied to the PC and the Windows user
deep.body: A saved licence works for this PC and this Windows user. Reinstalling Windows on the same account does not need a new key. A different PC, or a changed Windows account, asks for the key again.

deep.heading: Moving to a new PC
deep.body: Use Deactivate on the old PC if you can, so the key is free. If the new PC refuses the key as already used, contact support and say which PC the key was used on.

deep.heading: What Settings shows afterwards
deep.body: In current builds the gear shows License Active and hides the key box, because activation already happened at start-up.

examples.title: First start after installing
examples.result: The app opens. If your internet is down it says it saved an offline activation.

examples.title: Switch to a new PC
examples.goal: Use the same key on a new computer

settings.New PC: Enter the same key at start-up

examples.result: The key activates on the new PC. If refused as already used, contact support.

faq.q: Can I work offline?
faq.a: Yes once activated. If the licence service cannot be reached at activation, the app saves an offline activation.

faq.q: Why does it ask for my key again?
faq.a: You are on a different PC or Windows account, or the saved licence file was removed.

faq.q: Where do I buy a key?
faq.a: The same licence window has a Buy License button.

faq.q: Is my key included in a problem report?
faq.a: No. Report a Problem never includes it.

faq.q: Is there a cracked or free version?
faq.a: I cannot help with cracked copies: the app checks your licence key online. Buy License opens the store page; licence and error message questions go to support (Settings gear > Report a Problem).

mistakes.cause: A typo or extra spaces when pasting
mistakes.fix: Copy it again from your receipt and paste without spaces.

mistakes.symptom: You post a screenshot with your key in it
mistakes.cause: The key is visible in the licence window
mistakes.fix: Never share the key. Hide it before sending screenshots.

protips: Keep the email or receipt with your key somewhere safe. It is the only way to reactivate on a new PC.

articles.title: Bleed Paint Past Panel Edges (Edge Bleed): fewer seams in iRacing
articles.summary: Bleed Paint Past Panel Edges (Edge Bleed) is a checkbox in the Settings gear, under Options. It copies each panel’s edge paint and spec a few pixels into the gaps next to it, so far-away cars show fewer seam lines in iRacing; it is off by default and saves with your project.
articles.what: iRacing draws your paint from one flat sheet that holds the car cut into panels, with unused gaps between them. The sim shrinks that sheet for cars in the distance, so each panel’s edge picks up whatever sits in the gap next to it, and a faint line can show along the seams. Edge Bleed copies the paint and spec of each panel edge about 16 pixels into the gap beside it, so the shrunk sheet blends into your paint instead of the gap colour. Only gap pixels near a panel change; the panels themselves are never touched. It needs a car whose template has the panel outlines (the Wire layer). A flat picture with no outlines is left as it is, and the box says so.
when: You see thin lines along the panel edges of your car in iRacing from a distance.
You want to switch Edge Bleed on or off, or check that it is saved with your project.
how: 1. Open the Settings gear at the top right and look under Options.
2. Tick Bleed Paint Past Panel Edges. The line under it says how many panels it found.
3. Render as usual. The paint and spec files carry the bleed.
4. Untick it to go back to plain gaps. The choice is remembered, and Save Project keeps it with the project.

controls.label: Bleed Paint Past Panel Edges
controls.effect: Copies each panel’s edge paint and spec a few pixels into the gaps beside it.

tips: Turn it on once for a livery that shows thin lines along its panel edges in iRacing.
Judge it in iRacing from a distance, not up close.
pitfalls: It does not fix a thin line where your zones leave the template’s own outline in the catch-all colour.
A flat picture with no panel outlines cannot be bled; the box says so and the render is unchanged.
aliases: how do i use edge bleed
bleed paint past the panel edges

deep.heading: What changes in the files
deep.body: Only gap pixels within about 16 pixels of a panel, in the paint file and the spec file (and the night spec if you render one). Panel pixels are never touched, and gap further than that from every panel stays as it was.

deep.heading: Saved with the project
deep.body: Save Project keeps whether Edge Bleed is on and its pixel reach, and opening the project brings it back exactly, including off. A project saved before this simply opens without the setting. A crash restore keeps it too.

examples.title: Thin lines along the doors from far away
examples.result: The next render copies each panel edge into the gap next to it, and the lines at a distance fade.

faq.q: What is Edge Bleed?
faq.a: A checkbox in the Settings gear that copies each panel’s edge paint and spec a few pixels into the gaps beside it, so far-away cars show fewer seam lines in iRacing.

faq.q: Where is Edge Bleed?
faq.a: Open the Settings gear at the top right and look under Options for Bleed Paint Past Panel Edges.

faq.q: Is Edge Bleed on by default?
faq.a: No. It is off until you tick it, and Shokker remembers your choice.

faq.q: Does Edge Bleed change my paint on the car?
faq.a: No. Only the gap pixels next to a panel change. The panels themselves are never touched.

faq.q: Does Save Project keep Edge Bleed?
faq.a: Yes. Save Project keeps whether it is on and how far it reaches, and opening the project brings it back.

mistakes.symptom: Edge Bleed says it cannot read the panel outlines
mistakes.cause: The paint is a flat picture or a car without a Wire layer, so there are no outlines to read.
mistakes.fix: Open the layered template. Until then the render is unchanged.
